validator: draft 1 passes (no problems, soft or warnings); the faults below are the critic's.
keep: The idea is named in one line up front (integrating is differentiating run backwards: given a rate, find the rule it came from) [1], and the reverse rule is built from what Dan has, the power rule's two steps undone in the opposite order: add one to the power, then divide by the new power [3], with the one power it cannot do, −1, and why (it would divide by 0) [4].

The + c is taught from its cause, a constant differentiates to zero [2], and shown on the family of curves: the slider for c lifts the curve while the tangent at x = 2 keeps slope 4. The examiners' finding on the constant [7] is the misconception the course brief names for this lesson, and steps 8, 10, 11 and 12 each catch it with a wrong option of its own.

One fully worked example with real numbers from the rule, run backwards from i5's own charge rule q = 0.5t²: i = t amps, q = 0.5t² + c, 3 C at 0 s gives c = 3, 11 C at 4 s, checked both ways; and a known value at 2 s (5 C) giving the same c, so a starting value need not be at zero [5][6].

Twelve screens alternate SHOW (1, 3, 5, 7, 9) and DO (2, 4, 6, 8, 10), then mixed puzzles (11, 12), each wrong option a named slip with its number: not dividing, dividing by the old power, differentiating instead, no c, the 2t left as it was, a later value taken as c. All numbers checked by hand: 4, 0; 3; 4, 4/3; 2x³ + 2x² + 5x; x⁴ − 3x² + 2x, 12x² − 6; 4, 4 + c; 3, 8, 11, 5 → 3; 19, 9, 16; c = 5, 6x³ − 4x² + 3; c = 1, 9, 10, 8; hoist c = 1, 13 m.

The cable-tray analogy is from Dan's trade, reproduces the main result (one fall fits a tray at any height; one known height picks it) and its breaks is true (a tray's fall is constant, a curve's slope is not).
fix: Causal step skipped (fault 1): the reverse rule is checked only for x². Add the general check in one clause: differentiating xⁿ⁺¹ ÷ (n + 1) brings the n + 1 to the front and takes one off the power, (n + 1)xⁿ ÷ (n + 1) = xⁿ, so the two steps cancel for every power the rule allows.

Causal step skipped (fault 1): 'adding a number lifts every point by the same amount, so the steepness does not change' skips why. Say it from the chord Dan knows from lesson 1: a chord between any two points has both ends lifted by c, so its rise and therefore its slope are unchanged, and so is the tangent's.

Recommended shape, the misconception shown failing: the explain says leaving out c is a slip but never shows it going wrong. In the capacitor example, show q = 0.5t² without c giving 0 C at the start instead of the 3 C it held, and 8 C at 4 s instead of 11 C.

Faithful to the source (fault 2's cousin, a widened claim): 'Leaving out the + c is a well-known slip' says more than quote [7], which reports basic errors in dealing with the constant. Word it as errors with the constant, and keep 'many' and 'Advanced Higher'.
verdict: Rewrite as draft 2 with these four fixes; nothing else needs to change.
